items.english: By now the only thing on his mind was the weather. Wondering when the rain would ever come, he looked up at the sky and hobbled along behind them all, hop hop, pitched to be heard by whoever he could not make out in the dim road,
"Tiger—monkey—pig, tonight it has been nothing but animal talk, eh."
"And your frogs besides," came the answer, and it was the knowledge-face man.

Thinking suddenly of the nervous one from the konnyaku question and answer, he could hear voices chatting away ahead with the Tenjin-sama fellow. Presently they passed the woods of the Invalids Home, and in another step or two was the mouth of his own row house alley.
notes: I took the voices ahead to be the nervous student-like man talking with the Tenjin-like man, but the subject is left vague so I kept it vague. I kept konnyaku question and answer literal rather than explaining the joke.

items.english: "This back in here is where I live, it is a squalid hole, but if you are ever passing please step in," he said, taking his leave of them all. But he had one thing left he wanted to say, so he took one step forward and added, "And my plot, if you peep past the trifoliate orange hedge just there you will see it. It is dark now so you will not see well, but eggplants and cucumbers will be coming on plenty from now, more than the family alone can ever eat,"
notes: Kikokugaki is the trifoliate orange hedge around his plot. I kept it as a plain plant name without gloss.
Kept as silence in the text: no answer comes to the vegetable offer.

items.english: "Well, gentlemen, I will take my leave here."

The row house folk, who seemed already to be waiting even now for the eggplants and cucumbers to come, were all fast asleep. And the only one to greet this Edoya Nekohachi on his way home was the dog kept by the neighbourhood sake shop. But even to himself it seemed rare to be feeling so humble, and so human, as tonight.
notes: Edoya Nekohachi is his full house name, claimed here on the way home. I kept it unvaried rather than smoothing it to Nekohachi.

data.say: Drafted p178 to p185 keeping the garden farewell and its flat silence unlyrical.
